domestic.debt_note: Fresh MTB auction settled today, 2026-08-20: govt raised Rs498bn vs a Rs500bn target (~Rs2.1tn in total bids), with cutoffs UP across every tenor vs the 2026-08-05 auction -- 1M 11.47% (+12bp), 3M 11.65% (+13bp), 6M 11.80% (+10bp), 12M 11.99% (+4bp) -- sourced this run via https://tribune.com.pk/story/2624826/govt-raises-rs498b-via-t-bills-as-yields-rise. PIB 10Y remains anchored at the 2026-08-04 fixed-rate cutoff of 12.30% (no newer PIB auction found this run). The curve stays inverted above the held 11.5% policy rate -- a defensive carry cushion for T-bill/PIB-heavy bank books -- and is now WIDENING slightly, a mild signal that the market wants a touch more compensation even as SBP holds.

drivers: KSE-100 closed 2026-08-19 (Wednesday) at 176,846.36, down 1,109.14 points (-0.62%) -- a second down day but a much smaller one than 2026-08-18's -1.41% (177,955.51 close); the session opened higher on the gas circular-debt settlement news, hit an intraday high of 178,942.31, then gave it back to afternoon selling down to an intraday low of 176,638.10 -- sourced this run via https://www.brecorder.com/news/40435530/psx-kse-100-settles-1100-points-lower-amid-late-selling

IMPACT-4 fuel move effective 2026-08-20: petrol +Rs2.97/litre to Rs337.51 (partly funding a new Rs5/litre petroleum development levy tied to the circular-debt plan below); HSD diesel CUT Rs32.63/litre (-8.2%) to Rs363.06 despite global crude staying near 3-week highs -- an administrative intervention, not a market move: PM Shehbaz personally directed the petroleum minister to negotiate with refineries, who agreed to absorb the cut after two-three virtual meetings -- sourced this run via https://tribune.com.pk/story/2624845/pm-push-brings-steep-rs32-diesel-price-cut and https://mmnews.tv/petrol-and-diesel-prices-for-thursday-august-20-2026/. Net read: the diesel cut is disinflationary for freight/logistics/transport-heavy costs (diesel dominates trucking, which feeds broad CPI, especially food), a genuine near-term positive that reinforces the July CPI deceleration -- but it does not reduce the underlying Brent-driven import-bill/PKR risk, since crude itself has not fallen.

Government unveiled a plan to settle Rs1.49tn of Pakistan's Rs3.6tn gas-sector circular debt (Cabinet Committee on Energy, chaired by PM Shehbaz, 2026-08-19): Rs540bn via extra dividends from OGDC/PPL/Government Holdings, Rs270bn via the new Rs5/litre PDL -- a specific earnings catalyst for the listed E&P majors, though a same-day separate report flagged total ENERGY-sector circular debt (gas+power) has actually WIDENED to ~Rs5.29tn in FY26, so the fiscal overhang is only partially addressed -- sourced this run via https://propakistani.pk/2026/08/19/govt-unveils-plan-to-clear-rs-1-49-trillion-gas-circular-debt/ and https://www.nation.com.pk/19-Aug-2026/energy-sector-circular-debt-widens-nearly-rs5-3-trillion-fy2025-26

SBP held the policy rate at 11.5% on 2026-07-27 (second consecutive FY27 hold), citing inflation and Middle East risk even as it expects CPI to keep moderating after September; next MPC decision 2026-09-14 -- reconfirmed this run via https://tribune.com.pk/story/2620561/sbp-keeps-policy-rate-unchanged-at-115-1
